key_insight: Combines open-vocabulary semantic understanding of functional scene elements with contact-aware 3D human pose generation so models can produce plausible, functionality-driven human–scene interactions from language and scene input.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between recognizing object function in 3D scenes and generating realistic human poses that physically and semantically interact with those objects — preventing implausible or non-functional placements.
method: Open-vocabulary semantic grounding: map free-form language and scene geometry to functional element labels/affordances (e.g., 'sit-able', 'graspable') using language–vision priors.
Contact-aware pose generation: produce 3D human poses conditioned on scene geometry and predicted functional regions, enforcing plausible contact points and body support constraints.

Joint optimization/conditioning pipeline: combine scene semantics, contact priors and pose generation (learning-based or diffusion/optimization) to synthesize interactions that respect both function and physical plausibility.
impact: Enables more realistic, controllable 3D human–scene synthesis for embodied AI, robotics, and content creation pipelines, improving downstream tasks like simulation, virtual staging, and human-centered scene understanding.
visual_elements: Diagram: pipeline showing language + scene input → functional element detection → contact-aware pose generator → final 3D human-scene interaction
Before/after comparisons: examples where baseline methods produce implausible poses vs. this method producing functionally correct interactions (e.g., sitting, reaching)
Heatmap overlay: predicted functional affordance regions on a 3D scene mesh (e.g., sit-able, place-able, graspable)
Contact visualization: skeletons with highlighted contact points and support forces to show physical plausibility
paper_authors: Jie Liu, Yu Sun, Alpar Cseke, Yao Feng, Nicolas Heron
